layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract—Recent work on curvilinear structure segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has mostly focused on backbone network design and loss engi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neering. The challenge of collecting labelled data, an expensive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and labor intensive process, has been overlooked. While labelled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data is expensive to obtain, unlabelled data is often readily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available. In this work, we propose SemiCurv, a semi-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning (SSL) framework for curvilinear structure segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is able to utilize such unlabelled data to reduce the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labelling burden. Our framework addresses two key challenges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in formulating curvilinear segmentation in a semi-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manner. First, to fully exploit the power of consistency based SSL,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we introduce a geometric transformation as strong data augmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation and then align segmentation predictions via a differentiable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverse transformation to enable the computation of pixel-wise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency. Second, the traditional mean square error (MSE)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on unlabelled data is prone to collapsed predictions and this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: issue exacerbates with severe class imbalance (significantly more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background pixels). We propose a N-pair consistency loss to avoid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trivial predictions on unlabelled data. We evaluate SemiCurv on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: six curvilinear segmentation datasets, and find that with no more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than 5% of the labelled data, it achieves close to 95% of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance relative to its fully supervised counterpart.

layout_dets.text: I. INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This article has supplementary downloadable material available at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: https://doi.org/10.1109/TIP.2022.3189823, provided by the authors.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications, including road crack segmentation, road seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation from satellite images and biomedical image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation (e.g. segmenting blood vessels and cells). Existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research into curvilinear structure segmentation has focused on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designing better network architectures [1], [2] or loss functions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g. topology loss [3], [4]) to better account for the specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature of curvilinear structures like connectivity and loop

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A major challenge in curvilinear structure segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that has received less attention is the need for a large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of labelled data to obtain good performance. In many

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases, acquiring such labelled data for segmentation tasks is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-trivial and sometimes requires expert labelling. More-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over, the fine detail present in curvilinear structures demands

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increased annotation effort in comparison to the coarse-grained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polygon-based annotation that is sufficient for general (object-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based) segmentation tasks. At the same time, we often have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: access to unlabelled data at very low cost. For example, road

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scanning vehicles are running everyday to collect road surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: photographs, satellites are collecting aerial images on a daily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: basis, and medical images are abundant from daily diagnoses.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This availability of unlablled data suggests the use of semi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised learning (SSL) approaches that are able to exploit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the unlabelled data to reduce the amount of labelled data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: required.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Much work in SSL has focused on semi-supervised classifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation [5], and far fewer works have studied the use of SSL for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation, much less curvilinear structure segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation. Existing SSL methods for semantic segmentation adopt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one of two approaches: 1) utilizing a Generative Adversarial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Network (GAN) to enforce that predicted segmentation maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are indistinguishable from real segmentation maps [6], [7]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or 2) enforcing consistency of predicted segmentation maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on unlabelled data between two augmented samples [8]-[10].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The first strategy still requires a considerable amount of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labelled data to train the GAN. In contrast, consistency-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches are able to work with much less labelled data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and are more promising in the low-label regime. Therefore,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we build upon the consistency-based approach towards semi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised segmentation in this work.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Even though previous work has developed methods for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-supervised segmentation, we argue that direct application

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of these methods to the curvilinear segmentation task is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sub-optimal for the following two reasons. First, the types

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of data augmentation used by state-of-the-art SSL methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for generic segmentation tasks has thus far been limited

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pixel-wise perturbations, including a mix-up of multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images [9], [10]. Pixel-wise perturbations do not create more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diverse geometric views of image data (e.g. vertical cracks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: will always remain vertical under pixel-wise perturbations),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and thus may not fully exploit the power of consistency

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based SSL. Moreover, mixing up images could shift the data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: away from the real data manifold (i.e. the mixed-up image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may not look real), potentially harming SSL as demonstrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in our experiments. Secondly, curvilinear structures typically

layout_dets.text: Fig. 1. Illustration of aligning augmented images. Two random augmentations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are applied to original image I, resulting in Î and ĩ. As pixel-to-pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correspondence is no longer available between Î and I, we apply additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverse transformation to align two augmented images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occupy a small fraction (often under 10% and as little as 1%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the datasets we considered) of the image compared to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background, leading to a severely class-imbalanced segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation target; this is unlike the more general semantic seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation datasets [11] considered by these existing methods.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As we will show, the class imbalance and sparsity leads

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a “collapsing" issue with the consistency loss used by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SSL methods, resulting in models predicting constant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outputs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We next describe the key improvements we make to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency-based SSL to address these challenges associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specifically with curvilinear segmentation tasks:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Differentiable affine transformation. First, we propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: affine transformations as data augmentation for curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. This augmentation is effective because of two reasons.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: First, images with curvilinear structures are often captured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from planar surfaces; this is characteristic of images of road

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surfaces, satellite images, and images of cells taken under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a microscope, to give a few examples. Hence, synthesizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novel viewpoints as augmentation by affine transformation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: valid [12]. Second, segmentation of curvilinear structures is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected to be affine equivariant: for instance, the notion of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack on a road surface should remain the same regardless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of rotation, translation or resizing of the image, unlike in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic segmentation tasks where the pose of an semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object is often fixed or subject to small variation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: One challenge with using affine transformations as data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: augmentation is that despite being more diverse, they pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hibit computing consistency loss at the pixel level between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two randomly augmented images because pixel-wise cor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respondence is not preserved during affine transformation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As illustrated in Fig. 1, supposing I and I are randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: augmented from I, there is no explicit pixel-wise corre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spondence between î and ī with which we can enforce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the predictions to be consistent. To address this alignment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: issue, we propose to employ an inverse affine transformation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: following the networks' predictions as illustrated in Fig. 2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With both forward and inverse transformations, the pixel-to-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel correspondence is restored, enabling the computation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pixel-wise consistency loss between student and teacher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models. We note that incorporating the inverse transformation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the networks requires it to be differentiable for gradients

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to backpropagate; as affine transformation is differentiable, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inverse transformation allows end-to-end learning as part of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: networks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2. Overview of SemiCurv, a semi-supervised learning framework for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curvilinear structure segmentation. We adopt a mean-teacher like architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for semi-supervised learning. i) We first propose a geometric transformation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the inverse transformation to allow stronger data augmentation. ii) To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: account for the severe class-imbalance issue, we employ Dice loss and N-Pair

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loss for labelled and unlabelled data respectively. iii) Spatial encoding is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further incorporated to capture spatial correlations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) N-pair consistency. As noted above, we observe that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: widely adopted consistency loss, mean square error (MSE),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is prone to a “collapsing" issue. Trivial solutions to minimize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the MSE on unlabelled data exist where both student and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teacher networks predict constant outputs. The introduction of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a non-learnable teacher model may partially address this issue,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but cannot guarantee in principle that a trivial solution is not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learned. Moreover, we notice that there are often far fewer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positive (foreground) pixels than negative ones (background)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in curvilinear structure datasets, suggesting the prior distri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bution is highly biased towards background. This imbalance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further encourages the trivial solution where the learned model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicts all background on the unlabelled data. To overcome

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this challenge, we propose to use an N-pair loss [13] to avoid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trivial predictions on unlabelled data, inspired by the recent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: success of contrastive learning [14], [15].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) Spatial coordinate encoding. Finally, there is clear spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity and correlation in curvilinear structure patterns,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in that positive pixels are spatially adjacent. Although topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was studied to improve connectivity [3], [4], they require

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully labelled ground-truth to provide topological supervision.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To exploit the spatial correlation prior, we propose to add

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatial coordinate encoding as features to all layers of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backbone segmentation network. To avoid the potential over-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fitting to absolute spatial coordinates [16], we encode spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjacency using a sinusoid function, which preserves spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjacency information while reducing risk of overfitting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In summary, our work makes the following contributions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We introduce a differentiable affine transformation to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully exploit the strength of consistency based semi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised learning for curvilinear image segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We provide insight into a "collapsing" issue with MSE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency loss defined on unlabelled data and propose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to use N-pair loss to mitigate this issue.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • To further capture the spatial correlation, we incorporate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sinusoid spatial encoding as additional features.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to investigate into curvilinear structure segmentation in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a semi-supervised fashion. We extensively benchmarked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods on six curvilin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ear segmentation datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: II. RELATED WORK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Curvilinear Structure Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We briefly review previous work on curvilinear structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation in the context of road segmentation from satellite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, medical image segmentation and crack detection in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pavements. Early work in road segmentation [17] used fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connected networks, but were soon followed by CNNs [18].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent work has built on the CNN approach, focusing on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designing deeper and wider networks and considering infor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation at multiple scales [19], [20]. In the medical imaging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: community, efforts have focused on further improving the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: popular UNet backbone [21], [22]. These fully supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods have shown to be competitive in delineating linear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures like membrane segmentation [23]. Progress in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area of crack segmentation proceeded in a similar trajectory,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where recent progress is due to improved backbone network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design [1], [24]. Orthogonal to the above, in this work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we address the semi-supervised learning setting to reduce the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amount of labelled data needed to train high performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models by exploiting unlabelled data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To model spatial correlation and connectivity in curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures, a few works have incorporated topological con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: straints when training the segmentation model. One study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utilized intermediate features from a VGG network to capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topological structure [4], while another work used concepts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from persistent homology to provide more principled topolog-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical features; this idea was implemented by defining a loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between ground-truth and predicted persistent diagrams [3],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which assumes access to ground-truth labels. In this work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we adopt a simpler approach by using positional encodings to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capture spatial correlation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Semi-Supervised Learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We briefly review the two genres of semi-supervised learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing (SSL) methods, namely the consistency-based SSL and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adversarial training based SSL; for a more complete review,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: please refer to [5]. Consistency-based SSL methods [25]–[27]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utilize the unlabelled data to constrain learning by enforcing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model's predictions on the unlabelled data to be consis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tent with a specified target. Consistency regularization was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: firstly introduced in the context of deep learning by [28].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To better exploit the power of ensemble learning [25] used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temporal ensembling of models' predictions as a target for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency. [26] further proposed to ensemble the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters over time to obtain more stable consistency targets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Different from the previously mentioned approaches, the VAT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method [27] proposed to enforce consistency of a model's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions with that on an adversarially perturbed input [29].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Orthogonal to the above, the MixMatch method [30] proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to interpolate between labelled and unlabelled samples to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diversify the training set. Due to the high accuracy of temporal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ensembling and low memory footprint, we adopted Mean

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Teacher [26] as the backbone framework. Another line of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works adapt generative adversarial training to semi-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning. Specifically, in the seminal work [31], a discriminator

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was introduced to distinguish generated samples from real

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ones and at the same time classify real samples into respective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: categories.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. Semi-Supervised Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Semi-Supervised learning has been applied to semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation to alleviate the expensive image anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation task. Following the adversarial training approach [31]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [32] first employed a discriminator to distinguish generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fake images from real ones to improve semi-supervised learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing. A conditional generative adversarial network (GAN)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was further employed by ensuring that a discriminator can-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not distinguish predicted segmentation masks on unlabelled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images from ground-truth segmentation masks (on the labelled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images) [6]; [7] further imposes cycle consistency (building

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on CycleGAN) to constrain the learning on unlabelled data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, under low labeled data training a GAN is prone to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instability and may not generalize well to unlabeled data. Fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowing the consistency-based SSL approaches, [9] proposed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enforce consistency between the segmentation predictions of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images subject to a MixUp augmentation, i.e. random crops of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the two images are superimposed and consistency is enforced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the segmentation predictions of respective patches. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context of medical image segmentation, a framework similar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to Mean Teacher has been applied to skin lesion and CT-scan

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation [33]. All these existing methods only consider

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data augmentations that are either pixel-wise perturbations [9]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or rotations that are multiples of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [33] with pairwise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency; such augmentations are not strong enough to fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exploit the power of consistency regularization. These works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also do not address the issue where the MSE loss used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enforce consistency is prone to collapse.

layout_dets.text: F. Dice Loss for Class Imbalance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It is well-known that class imbalance can affect the per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance of machine learning models [36]–[38]. The cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy (CE) loss commonly used for supervised segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks averages the pixel-wise CE loss over all pixels in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image; CE loss biases learning towards the majority class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when there is an imbalanced class distribution. In curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure segmentation tasks, this imbalance is particularly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: severe due to a low positive class ratio (see Table I). As a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result, models trained with CE may have high per-pixel accu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: racy but low intersection over union (IoU), which is the most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common evaluation metric for segmentation tasks. In order to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mitigate this issue, Dice loss [39] (Eq. 10) was proposed as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an alternative for segmentation; it focuses on the intersection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of predictions with ground truth only for the positive class.

layout_dets.text: IV. EXPERIMENTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We validate the efficacy of SemiCurv on 6 different curvi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A. Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CrackForest [40] was proposed for crack segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: for training, 10% for validation, and 10% for testing. Among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consisting of 1896/348/1124 labelled road crack images for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training, validation, and testing respectively. We follow the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standard datasplit proposed in [1] and assume the training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set is partially labelled. Gaps384 [1] was created from a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large road crack detection dataset GAPS [41] by manually

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selecting 384 images and cropping out smaller regions with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cracks, totalling 508 annotated images. We follow the standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In total, we obtain 6880/1215/440 labelled images for training,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: B. Evaluation Metric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To evaluate the quality of segmentation predictions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we compute Intersection over Union (IoU) using a threshold

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 0.5 on prediction posteriors for all test images and report

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mean IoU. We also evaluate the F1 measure of precision

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and recall at threshold 0.5. This metric treats segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a binary classification task. For all 6 datasets, we set the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background pixel label as 0 and foreground as 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C. Competing Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We extensively compare SemiCurv with existing fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised methods (with different backbone networks) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art generic semi-supervised learning methods,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as described in the following.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Fully Supervised Methods: We first investigate the state-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of-the-art fully supervised curvilinear structure segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge detection, and semantic segmentation methods. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provides context of what is achievable for curvilinear seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation tasks. FPHBN [1] is the state-of-the-art method for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crack segmentation; we used the reported results on Crack500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in this paper for comparison. HED [44] was proposed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detecting edges in images. Due to the similar nature of edge

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and linear structures defined in this work, we evaluate this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: backbone as a baseline. DeepLab v3+ [45] is the state-of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the-art backbone network for semantic segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate this network here to show that generic semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation networks do not generalize well to curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure segmentation. UNet [21] was originally proposed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for medical image segmentation. We use a variant that adds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: residual connections in each convolution block as the back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bone network in this work. Details of the backbone network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is given in the Supplementary Material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Semi-Supervised Methods: We compare against state-of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the-art semi-supervised semantic segmentation, medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, and generic SSL methods adapted to curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. CutMix [9] proposed to generate random mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to mix two images and consistency is applied to between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the predictions of teacher model and student model over

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the masked regions. TCSM [33] adapts the mean teacher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework to learn from unlabelled data. The augmentation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited to scaling and rotation in multiples of 90°. VAT [27]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed to learn the optimal augmentation by maximiz-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the consistency on unlabelled data. The final objective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aims to minimize the pairwise consistency as well as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy on unlabelled data. cGAN [46] is another line of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-supervised semantic segmentation approach. The condi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional GAN (cGAN) based method introduced a discriminator

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network to differentiate ground-truth segmentation mask from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicted ones and the predictions on unlabeled data can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be constrained by the discriminator. Mean Teacher (Base-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: line) [26] proposed to use a temporal ensemble, as teacher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a learnable student model to provide pseudo labels to train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the student model. MSE consistency is used between teacher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and student outputs. We use this as our baseline method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SemiCurv is our proposed model incorporating differentiable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geometric transformations, N-pair objective, and sinusoid posi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional encoding.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1) Supervised Loss: We first compare the supervised loss,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SupLoss, adopted for labelled images. UNet with weighted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binary cross entropy loss, WBCE, is consistently worse than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UNet with dice loss, Dice. This suggests that optimizing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dice loss is able to better generalize under severe class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imbalance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2) Semi-Supervised Learning: We next compare the fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised baseline with the mean teacher model, MT. With

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mean square error (MSE) consistency loss, we observe signifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cant improvement of MT over the baseline. We further evaluate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MT with and without the differentiable geometric transfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation, GeoTform. The significant difference in performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the two settings indicates that strong augmentation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vital to the success of consistency-based SSL.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) MSE vs N-Pair Consistency Loss: We further compare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MT with mean square error loss, MSE, and N-pair loss.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The improvement demonstrates the superiority of considering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both positive and negative pairs simultaneously with N-pair.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In addition to the numerical improvement, we also show in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 8 (a) that N-pair is more robust than MSE and avoids

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: collapsed predictions. As we discussed in Sect. III-D, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pairwise mean square error, MSE, consistency loss is prone to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: collapsing issue. This becomes severe when the data is highly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imbalanced and very few labelled samples are available for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training. We present examples for both MSE consistency and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N-pair consistency on CrackForest with only 1% labelled data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 8 (a). MSE produces unstable validation performance,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and it eventually collapses to all zeros around 800 epochs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In contrast, with the proposed N-pair loss the validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance keeps stable throughout the training. Overfitting,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to too few labelled data, is still observed but it avoids

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: collapsing to all zero predictions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4) Positional Encodings: We analyze the effect of including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various forms of spatial encoding. First, when including linear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatial encoding, Linear Spt. Enc., we sometimes observe that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance degrades. This can be attributed to the potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overfitting to absolute locations; using sinusoid spatial encod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing instead, Sinusoid Spt. Enc., we observe clear and consistent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvements on all datasets. We investigate the impact of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constant K in Eq. 9 which controls the period of sinusoid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: positional encoding. The final SemiCurv is evaluated with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: K = 1, 2, 4, 8 with results shown in Fig. 8 (b). We observe an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimal range of K around 4, and overall the results are robust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to K from 2 to 8. This shows sinusoid positional encoding is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a robust component of our approach.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For alternative positional encodings, we evaluate two addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional methods on CrackForest segmentation task. The results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are presented in Tab. IV. We observe a small drop of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance when swapping out our proposed sinusoid encod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing with learned position embedding [35] and rotary posi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion embedding [47]. Overall, the proposed sinusoid position

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoding is still the better option.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5) Alternative Similarity Metric: We further explore a dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferent option for the similarity metric used in the N-pair loss.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L2 distance is often used in N-pair loss for metric learning and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we therefore evaluated the induced RBF kernel for comparison

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against cosine similarity. Formally, the L2 distance induced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similarity is given by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The quantitative comparison between using cosine similarity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and L2 distance induced similarity is shown in Table V

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under the similarity metric (Sim.) column. For both similarity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics, we use the SemiCurv framework and keep the training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protocols unchanged. We observe from the comparison that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cosine similarity outperforms L2 distance consistently on all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets. Also, stability of training suffers with L2 distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compared to SemiCurv with cosine distance. This can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attributed to the normalizing effect of cosine similarity, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L2 distance is affected by the absolute number of positive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel predictions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7) Exponential Moving Averaging Hyperparameter: We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: choose the EMA hyperparameter for teacher model according

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the validation performance. A lower α will allow faster

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: update of teacher network while a higher α slows down the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: update of teacher network. This hyperparameter is particu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larly sensitive for MSE consistency loss according because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MSE loss is more likely to produce collapsed prediction, i.e.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicting all pixels as background. In this section we further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide empirical evidence for the chosen hyperparameter α

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by varying α from 0.9 to 0.9999 and compare the performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on CrackForest dataset. The results in Fig. 6 suggest choosing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: α = 0.999 is the optimal choice for both mean teacher and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our SemiCurv models.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: F. Qualitative Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We further present qualitative comparisons of UNet, Cut-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mix, MT, and SemiCurv on 4 datasets in Fig. 7. We make

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the following observations: first, for both MT and SemiCurv,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the visual quality of segmentation results are more appealing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and better mimicks the ground-truth compared to the fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised baseline UNet. In particular, our method is able to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate more well-connected predictions for 037 (1st row)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thanks to the contribution of appending positional encod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing. We further notice that SemiCurv produces, in general,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cleaner outputs for 037 (1st row), 022 (2nd row), 066_1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (3rd row). We also observe, in 0192_541_1 (4th row), the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed approach captures very subtle cracks on the top. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation results on DRIVE dataset (5th/6th rows) also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suggest the superiority of SemiCurv. It produces relatively high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fidelity and well-delineated blood vessel segmentation maps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In comparison, UNet, CutMix, and MT tend to mingle different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blood vessels together which is less common in SemiCurv's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions. For satellite image segmentation, the visualization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: covers industrial areas (row 7) and rural areas (rows 8-9).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We observe consistent improvements of SemiCurv compared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to both UNet and state-of-the-art semi-supervised image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation CutMix. Interestingly, the SemiCurv predictions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: V. CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work we addressed curvilinear structure segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion in a semi-supervised learning setting to exploit “freely"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available and abundant amounts of unlabelled data with our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed SemiCurv framework. In particular, we introduced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stronger augmentation involving affine geometric transfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mations which we showed to be essential to the success

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SSL. We further identified implications of the severe class

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imbalance in curvilinear segmentation tasks on the widely used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MSE consistency loss, and showed that N-pair loss should be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used instead to mitigate these issues. Finally, we found that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sinusoid positional encoding is effective in further improv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing segmentation performance. Our extensive experiments on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 curvilinear structure segmentation datasets from 3 different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domains demonstrates the effectiveness of SemiCurv, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detailed ablation studies validated the importance of each of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our proposed components. Our SemiCurv framework and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extensive results presented in this work provide a foundation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for future work in SSL for curvilinear segmentation.
